dublinCore.title: Frequency Detection
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Fourier transform
Frequency detection
Winding machine
Center of mass
Aliasing
dublinCore.description: A winding machine: a sampled sine wave is wrapped around a circle that spins with an adjustable period. A polar plot shows the wound curve, a panel shows its center of mass, and a frequency-strength graph plots the distance of the center of mass from the origin against the circle period, peaking when the circle period equals the signal period. AutoPoll sweeps the circle period from 0.1 to 2 s.

topic: Winding a signal around a circle
learningObjectives: Explain how winding a signal around a spinning circle turns it into a center of mass whose distance from the origin measures the strength of one frequency
Predict that the center of mass stays about 0.5 from the origin only when the circle period equals the signal period, and keeps returning to the origin otherwise
Interpret the AutoPoll frequency-strength graph to find the period and frequency of a sine wave
Relate the center-of-mass average to the Fourier transform integral X(f) = integral of x(t) e^{-i 2 pi f t} dt
Identify an alias peak caused by a low resolution (sampling rate) and compute where it appears
prerequisites: Period and frequency of a sinusoid
Center of mass of a set of points

misconceptions.misconception: The horizontal axis of the frequency-strength graph is frequency
misconceptions.correction: It is the circle period Tc; the frequency 1/Tc decreases to the right, and the header converts the peak to hertz
misconceptions.evidence: A 0.8 s signal (1.25 Hz) peaks to the right of a 0.5 s signal (2 Hz)

misconceptions.misconception: Only the exactly matching period gives a large center of mass
misconceptions.correction: Nearby periods look matched for a while; separating close frequencies needs a long observation (spectral leakage)
misconceptions.evidence: With Ts = 0.5 s and Tc = 0.55 s, |COM| is 0.49 after 1 s and 0.17 after 4 s, and reaches zero only at 5.5 s

dependencies: Inconsolata font (frequency-detection.otf, SIL Open Font License)

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Frequency detection by winding. A sine wave with an adjustable period is wrapped around a circle that spins with an adjustable period. A polar plot shows the wound curve, a panel shows its center of mass and its distance from the center, and a graph plots that distance against the circle period. Play winds the signal; AutoPoll sweeps the circle period from 0.1 to 2 seconds.

colorScheme.accent: blue period markers, yellow center of mass, red current sample

controls.label: Circle period
controls.description: Sets Tc, the time for one turn of the winding circle; aligned under the shared 0-2 s axis of the graphs

controls.label: Signal period
controls.description: Sets Ts, the period of the sine wave being analyzed; changing it clears the frequency-strength graph

controls.label: Resolution
controls.description: Samples per second of simulated time (the sampling rate); low values produce aliasing

controls.label: Speed
controls.description: Multiplies the rate at which simulated time advances

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Stops the winding, erases the wound curve and clears the frequency-strength graph

controls.label: AutoPoll
controls.description: Sweeps the circle period from 0.10 to 2.00 s in 0.05 s steps at 20x speed, recording each strength once it settles; press again to stop

controls.label: Show Spin
controls.description: Rotates the polar drawing with the circle so the current sample moves straight up and down

visualElements.description: Frequency Strength: |center of mass| (0 to 1) against circle period (0 to 2 s), one yellow stem per measured period, with the peak period and frequency in the header
Cartesian Coordinates: the next 2 s of the sampled sine wave, with blue lines at each completed turn of the circle
Polar plot of the wound curve with the current sample in red
Center of Mass panel: the wound curve with its center of mass (yellow) and the |COM| read-out

model.description: Sample n (t = n/R) of x(t) = sin(2 pi t / Ts) is placed at radius -x and angle 2 pi t / Tc; the strength is the distance of the average of all placed points from the origin
equations: |COM| = |(1/M) sum z_n| = |(1/M) sum x(t_n) e^{-i 2 pi f_c t_n}|, f_c = 1/Tc
algorithms: AutoPoll: step Tc by 0.05 s once successive per-period strengths change by less than 0.01

instructionalStrategies: Use AutoPoll to detect an unknown period
extensions: Add a second sine component and look for two peaks
Add a DC offset to the signal and predict where its strength belongs (zero frequency, an infinitely long circle period)
